title: Medicare use and payment by county, against the rest of California
question: In which Bay Area counties and kinds of service does Medicare pay far more per user than in the middle California county, or has payment grown far faster than in the State?
finding: Of 143 county and service lines for the six Bay Area counties in 2025, 6 stand out. The clearest is independent diagnostic testing facility pt b in Marin County: $3.8 million in 2025, 6.1 times the 2020 figure of $628,566 (the State grew 1.3 times), $965 per user against $421 in the middle California county. Statewide, California had 2.8 hospices for every 10,000 people in traditional Medicare in 2025 against 1.3 nationally (813 hospices in 2020, 1,157 in 2025), and 6.0 home-health agencies against 2.1.
how: From the federal market saturation file, calendar years 2020 to 2025, for every kind of service it covers. Each Bay Area county's payment per user is set against the middle California county with 100 or more users, and its growth in total payment since 2020 against the State's. A line is listed when payment is $1 million or more and either the per-user figure is 1.5 times the middle county, or payment at least tripled and grew at least twice as fast as the State. Counts of providers per 10,000 people compare California with the country, using State and national rows only.
limits: County figures count the providers that served people living in the county, wherever the provider is, so county provider counts cannot be compared with State totals. Payment rates that differ by area would lift every Bay Area line somewhat. A single new imaging or testing company, or a national one that begins billing for county residents, can move a small county's line a great deal. The file counts fee-for-service (traditional) Medicare only. The dialysis facility reports on disk hold clinical measures, not payments or ownership, and were read but not screened; nothing in the county dialysis line stands out.

rows.service: Independent Diagnostic Testing Facility Pt B
